title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Furman customs, ceremonies, and recurring campus events—from first-year orientation to Homecoming and finals.

cards.title: LDOC Senior Splash
cards.subtitle: Last Day of Classes • Furman fountain
cards.notes: If you are a graduating senior, check university guidance for the year’s LDOC plans and observe the fountain celebration from an appropriate public area.
cards.short_summary: Graduating seniors mark the last day of classes with a fountain splash.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman identifies seniors splashing in the fountain on LDOC as a tradition; its account describes it as a senior rite of passage.
cards.access_notes: Annual timing and participation guidance may vary; consult current university communications.

cards.title: Listen for “FU All the Time”
cards.subtitle: Furman athletics
cards.notes: At a game, follow the cheerleaders and event staff for the appropriate time to join the school cheer; keep the focus on positive, respectful support.
cards.short_summary: A Furman cheer associated with former president John E. Johns.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman lists the “FU All the Time” cheer as having been made famous by former president John E. Johns, who often led it during third quarters of games.
cards.access_notes: Occurs in the context of athletic events; check the current game schedule and venue policies.

cards.title: Homecoming Carnival on the Mall
cards.subtitle: Homecoming • Furman Mall
cards.notes: Check the published Homecoming schedule before going; the official tradition page describes carnival activities on Furman Mall during the weekend.
cards.short_summary: An annual Homecoming carnival with rides and activities on Furman Mall.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman describes its Homecoming carnival as an annual event on Furman Mall, with food, rides, and a bouncy castle.
cards.access_notes: Event details and admission terms vary by year; consult the current Homecoming schedule.

cards.title: Build a Homecoming Float
cards.subtitle: Homecoming • Furman Mall
cards.notes: If your organization participates, confirm its plans and work during the scheduled Mall session; the winners are announced at Saturday halftime.
cards.short_summary: A campuswide Homecoming float contest presented by FUSAB.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman’s Homecoming page calls float building a campuswide tradition, presented by FUSAB, with winners announced at halftime on Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Scheduling and organization participation vary by year; verify the current Homecoming program.

cards.title: Homecoming Bonfire and Pep Rally
cards.subtitle: Homecoming • Milford Mall
cards.notes: Use the current Homecoming schedule for location and timing, and follow all event-staff directions around the bonfire and pep-rally area.
cards.short_summary: A Furman Homecoming tradition led with cheerleaders and team captains.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman’s Homecoming page identifies the pep rally and bonfire as a tradition, led by Furman cheerleaders with appearances by the football team captains.
cards.access_notes: Event schedule and site controls vary by year; follow on-site safety instructions.

cards.title: Moonlight Breakfast Before Finals
cards.subtitle: End of each semester
cards.notes: Look for the dining announcement near finals; the university describes faculty and staff serving the breakfast event at each semester’s end.
cards.short_summary: Faculty and staff serve a late-semester breakfast event for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman states that Moonlight Breakfast occurs at the end of each semester and is served by faculty and staff to help students prepare for finals.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current semester’s dining announcement, location, and eligibility before attending.

cards.title: Start With the First-Year Walk
cards.subtitle: Orientation • PAC to McAlister Auditorium
cards.notes: Incoming students should follow the orientation schedule and staff directions for the procession from the PAC to McAlister Auditorium.
cards.short_summary: First-years walk to Opening Convocation at the start of their Furman experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman’s admissions blog describes incoming students walking from the PAC to McAlister Auditorium for commencement/convocation, with the route echoed at graduation.
cards.access_notes: Available to the entering class when included in the current orientation program.

cards.title: Return Along Furman Mall at Commencement
cards.subtitle: Commencement • McAlister Auditorium to the PAC
cards.notes: Graduating students should rely on the current Commencement instructions for procession order, regalia, staging, guest access, and weather updates.
cards.short_summary: Graduates retrace the first-year route in academic regalia.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman describes graduates walking in regalia from McAlister Auditorium back along the same Mall route used by incoming students.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to the official Commencement procession; consult current Commencement materials.

cards.title: Orientation Singing at South Housing
cards.subtitle: Orientation • SOHO (South Housing)
cards.notes: If scheduled during orientation, follow Orientation Staff direction and residence-hall policies; treat it as a supervised welcome-week activity.
cards.short_summary: A welcome-week singing custom staged below South Housing balconies.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman’s admissions blog reports that Orientation Staff have organized first-years to sing to South Housing balconies during orientation week.
cards.access_notes: This is orientation-program dependent; do not enter residence halls or disturb residents outside official programming.

cards.title: See “Good Luck, Charlie” During Exams
cards.subtitle: Charlie Peace bust • James B. Duke Library
cards.notes: During exams, look for the library’s designated adornments rather than bringing objects yourself; respect library staff, displays, and quiet-study rules.
cards.short_summary: The Charlie Peace bust is dressed up as an exam-time good-luck custom.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman reports that during exam periods the bust of Charlie Peace in the library is adorned for good luck, with a basket of items now used for the tradition.
cards.source_title: Fact or Folklore?: Furman’s Urban Legends
cards.access_notes: Observe library procedures and any staff instructions for the display during exam periods.
